subject: Confirmatory Factor Analysis with non-normal data and categorial items - Which estimator?

messages.author: b0abe4cdc530bdde
messages.subject: Confirmatory Factor Analysis with non-normal data and categorial items - Which estimator?
parts:
I am trying to run a CFA on a dataset (n=276). I want to test a 3 factor-model on 9 items (Likert-scale from 0 to 10). As I have a non-normal data, I cannot use ML as estimator. However, I cannot decide which estimator I should use instead. I have read about Unweighted Least Squares, Weighted Least Squares (or Asymptotic Distribution Free), Robust Weighted Least Squares (WLSMV) and MLM (Satorra-Bentler).

First of all, I would really like to know which one is better and why.

And second, I would like to know what should I report for MLM and WLSMV as I have 2 columns in the summary (example here below for the MLM). There's also a robust CFI and a robust TLI (the ones above, in the column robust were not the robust ones?!).

I am a bit lost and your help would really be appreciated. Thank you  in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Confirmatory Factor Analysis with non-normal data and categorial items - Which estimator?
parts:
Likert-scale from 0 to 10)

With so many ordered categories, this is approximately continuous:
As I have a non-normal data, I cannot use ML as estimator
Yes you can, just use a robust correction.

However, I cannot decide which estimator I should use instead. I have read about Unweighted Least Squares, Weighted Least Squares (or Asymptotic Distribution Free), Robust Weighted Least Squares (WLSMV) and MLM (Satorra-Bentler).

First of all, I would really like to know which one is better and why.

You can't trust the SEs and test statistics from ULS, and you can only trust the ones from ADF if the sample size is in the thousands (you only have N=276), so avoid both of those.  WLSMV and MLM/MLR return similar results with so many ordered categories:

http://psych.colorado.edu/~willcutt/pdfs/Rhemtulla_2012.pdf

MLR has the advantage over MLM of being available even with missing data and you want to use FIML.  With complete data, MLM and MLR are asymptotically equivalent.
And second, I would like to know what should I report for MLM and WLSMV as I have 2 columns in the summary (example here below for the MLM).
Use the robust column, which provides the robust-corrections to the naïve statistics in the left column.
There's also a robust CFI and a robust TLI (the ones above, in the column robust were not the robust ones?!).

Those are only available with robust ML, but yes, refer to those instead of the "scaled" versions in the "Robust" column.  It is a little less confusing in the fitMeasures() output, which labels them as scaled vs. robust.  These articles explain why the Robust CFI, TLI, and RMSEA are better than simply calculating them using the scaled chi-squared value.

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2014.933697

http://dx.doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2012.715252

Terrence D. Jorgensen

Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
